config.description:
Configures the KiSS server {hostname} on {platform} with lines of its CLI, read the way Cisco IOS reads them. All lines of one call apply together or not at all, so batch related changes in one call; a call answers with what changed: the old line after -, the new one after +. Every default fits as it is, so set only what differs.
Commands: set <module> <key> [item] <value> | no <module> <key> [item] | no <module> <item> | show <module> [key] [item] | show running-config [all] | show startup-config | show diff <config> <config> | show version | show logging | show conversations | copy running-config startup-config | write [memory] | write erase | erase running-config | erase startup-config | erase conversations | erase <id>; erase conversations erases every conversation not pinned, erase <id> one conversation.
A key is two fixed words, a module then a key; a key of a collection such as endpoints takes the item name next; the value always comes last: set endpoints url openrouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1.
Modules, with their keys: {modules}.
A line that stops short lists what may follow it; show running-config all lists every key with its default; words abbreviate while only one word starts so (sh run); | include, exclude, begin or count <regexp> filters any output.
A secret never shows: show writes ! <module> <key> [item] is set for one that is set. To set one, write its line without the value, set endpoints key <name>: the user types it where you never see it, so never ask for it in the chat.
A new url, a copy, a write or an erase asks the user to confirm as the line runs: run the line, never ask in the chat first; a refused change stays refused, never reach it another way.
A route lets a page reach a url through this server, under the name of the item of the page: set proxy url <name> <url> here, and set proxy key <name> when the url needs a key, held here and never on the page; then set endpoints proxy <name> <backend> or set mcp proxy <name> <backend> on the page, <backend> the name of its mcp item for this server, the item keeping its own url and key unused; no endpoints proxy <name> or no mcp proxy <name> there sends it direct again.
Example call:
set proxy url openrouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
set proxy key openrouter
show proxy

view.description:
Supports viewing text, images, and directory listings on {hostname}.

Supported path types:
- Directories: Lists files and directories up to 2 levels deep, ignoring hidden items and the contents of node_modules
- Image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP): Displays the image visually
- Text files: Displays numbered lines. You can optionally specify a view_range to see specific lines.

modules.chat: the model this server answers with, endpoint/model, and its system prompt
modules.endpoints: the LLM APIs this server talks to
modules.files: the limits of view, str_replace and create_file
modules.mcp: the MCP servers whose tools this server calls, each tool taking tools use by its name, consent unless set
modules.models: the request parameters of an endpoint/model, each sent only when set
modules.proxy: the routes of this server, each relaying proxy/<name> to its url
modules.server: where it listens, its hostname, its key, its working directory, its logs
modules.shells: one tool per shell this machine has, named after it
modules.tools: each tool by its name here (bash, view, config): off hides it, consent asks the user at each call, on lets it run; max-rounds caps the tool rounds of a turn
